newsitem.title: CANADA: Environmental group drops Canada diamond mine case.
newsitem.headline: Environmental group drops Canada diamond mine case.

text.p: The World Wildlife Fund, an environmental group, said Monday it withdrew a court application that had sought judicial review of the government's approval of Canada's first Arctic diamond mine.

The mine is being built by Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd in a joint venture with Dia Met Minerals Ltd. The project received government approval last year after a long review and production is scheduled to begin in 1998.

World Wildlife Fund said it withdrew its court action filed last summer because the governments of Canada and the Northwest Territories in talks with the group committed to develop a strategy for protected areas in the territory and implement it by 2000.
Also, the government has told the group that future such environmental reviews must take into account projects' potential impact on the protected areas.
The group originally filed its application with the federal court in Toronto because it was unhappy with the environmental assessment procedure that the diamond mine proposal underwent.
